additions.sentence: The NHS advises calling NHS 111 if you often get headaches or blurred vision, if you have chest pain that comes and goes, or if you have other symptoms you think could be from high blood pressure.
additions.evidence: Search result: NHS advises 111 for frequent headaches/blurred vision, chest pain that comes and goes.

additions.sentence: Wearing a 24-hour ambulatory monitor is the preferred way to confirm high blood pressure, and home monitoring is used if an ambulatory monitor is unsuitable or not tolerated.
additions.evidence: NICE NG136 summary: ABPM preferred; HBPM if unsuitable or not tolerated.

additions.sentence: A reading taken in a clinic is less accurate than home or ambulatory readings and is not enough on its own to diagnose high blood pressure.
additions.evidence: NICE NG136: clinic measurement not alone adequate.

additions.sentence: About 1 in 4 people have higher readings at a GP surgery or clinic than at home.
additions.evidence: East Kent Hospitals leaflet: about 1 in 4 read higher in clinic.

additions.sentence: Most blood pressure medicines are taken as tablets once a day.
additions.evidence: Search summary of NHS treatment page: most taken as tablets once a day.

additions.sentence: Making lifestyle changes early on may mean some people can avoid needing medicine.
additions.evidence: NHS treatment page: by making these changes early you may be able to avoid medicines.

additions.sentence: Water tablets (diuretics) work by increasing the amount of salt the kidneys remove.
additions.evidence: Search 1 summary: diuretics increase salt kidneys remove (source blended, low confidence).

additions.sentence: Fewer than 1 in 20 people with high blood pressure have an underlying cause such as a kidney or adrenal gland condition.
additions.evidence: Search 1: in fewer than 1 in 20 cases there is an underlying cause (blended).
